2611.23165.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
2611.23165.abstract: Demonstrating a quantum advantage when solving large-scale computational problems on a quantum computer requires the correction of errors that occur due to limitations in control accuracy and coherence. Using the concept of quantum error correction, fault-tolerant logical qubits can be realized and manipulated with logical single- and two-qubit gates. In this paper, we experimentally analyze fault-tolerant lattice-surgery, which is a key primitive that enables operations between logical qubits realized in the surface-code. Using this primitive, we demonstrate the teleportation of logical states between two distance-three logical qubits realized in a superconducting circuit composed of 41 physical qubits. Throughout this process, we study the step-by-step transfer of logical information from a source to a target logical qubit by characterizing the time evolution of logical observables. We find that repeated execution of stabilizer measurements, after merging two surface-code patches, restores fault tolerance and yields increased fidelity of the teleported state. When optimizing the protocol in terms of gate count and sequence duration, we observe further improvements in fidelity. Our work offers new insights into the optimization of fault-tolerant lattice-surgery operations, while also providing a comprehensive description of the physical device and gate sequences used. We expect the efficient implementation of increasingly complex logical circuits to enhance the performance of future fault-tolerant quantum computers.
2611.23165.why: ETH teleports logical states between two distance-3 surface-code patches with lattice surgery on 41 qubits, tracking logical observables step by step.

eli5.plain: They moved encoded, error-protected quantum information from one block of qubits to another on a 41-qubit chip.
eli5.how: Two surface-code logical qubits are merged and split by measuring joint stabilizers (lattice surgery); they follow the logical state over time and show extra stabilizer rounds after merging restore fault tolerance.
eli5.matters: Lattice surgery is how surface-code machines will do two-qubit logic; this is a complete, documented demonstration on a mid-size superconducting device.
eli5.caveat: Distance three only corrects one error, and the teleportation fidelity is still limited by physical error rates rather than shown to improve with code size.

2611.21448.title: Plenitude of ideal correlations explains quantum theory
2611.21448.abstract: We show that the Hilbert-space formalism and the Born rule of quantum theory are singled out by the following principle: every correlation that is possible in a theory in which every observable admits an ideal measurement is physically realizable. An ideal measurement is one that yields the same outcome when repeated and does not disturb any compatible observable.
2611.21448.why: Cabello derives Hilbert space and the Born rule from one principle: every correlation allowed when all observables have ideal measurements is realized.

eli5.plain: They show that quantum theory's mathematical structure follows from one rule about which correlations nature allows.
eli5.how: Assume every observable can be measured ideally (repeatable, not disturbing compatible ones); then demand that every correlation such a theory permits actually occurs. Only Hilbert space with the Born rule fits.
eli5.matters: It is a compact answer to 'why this theory', built on measurement properties that experimentalists can test, including with qubits.
eli5.caveat: The 'plenitude' principle is strong and its physical motivation is debatable; the abstract gives the claim, not how loopholes are handled.

2611.21110.title: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
2611.21110.abstract: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing. In conventional cavity optomechanics, both the sign and the magnitude of the optical damping are dictated by the laser detuning, and cooling is bounded by quantum backaction (QBA), the optomechanical analogue of the Doppler limit in cold atoms. We show, in theory and experiment, that dynamical backaction can be strongly enhanced in multimode optomechanical resonators driven by time-varying (Floquet) optical fields. A modulated drive couples a sideband-unresolved MHz mode to a sideband-resolved GHz mode through the shared cavity, replacing the QBA limit of the target mode by the occupancy of the auxiliary mode. Experimentally, we cool the MHz mode to $47 \pm 13$ phonons, about half its single-mode QBA limit and an order of magnitude below what single-tone backaction reaches at the same intracavity photon number. The character of the interaction can moreover be completely inverted at fixed laser detuning, turning cooling into amplification and vice versa, controlled solely by the modulation frequency. Floquet driving thus extends open-loop quantum control, which requires no measurement or feedback, to mechanical resonators outside the resolved-sideband regime.
2611.21110.why: Floquet-modulated drive borrows a resolved-sideband GHz mode to cool a MHz mode below its quantum backaction limit, and flips cooling to amplification.

eli5.plain: They cooled a slow vibration below its usual quantum limit by wiggling the laser so the cooling is done through a second, faster vibration.
eli5.how: A modulated drive links an unresolved MHz mode and a resolved GHz mode in the same cavity, so the slow mode's limit becomes the fast mode's occupancy; the modulation frequency alone decides cooling versus amplification.
eli5.matters: Floquet-driven parametric coupling is exactly the toolbox of microwave optomechanics and cQED; open-loop control of backaction transfers directly.
eli5.caveat: Still 47 phonons, far from the ground state, and it relies on a well-chosen pair of mechanical modes.

2611.25053.title: Modeling couplings and quench dynamics of hundred-qubit quantum processors
2611.25053.abstract: Quantum processors now operate beyond the reach of exact classical simulation, yet their design and verification rest on precise models of the device. Understanding which properties of quantum processors can still be predicted on classical computers is central both to building these machines and to delimiting claims of quantum advantage. Here we address this question at the device level, using continuous unitary transformations to derive effective Hamiltonians non-perturbatively for two-dimensional superconducting processors at a cost polynomial in qubit number. For a 96-transmon array with tunable couplers, we extract the effective qubit couplings, state-dependent interactions (e.g., ZZ couplings), and eigenstate locality that guide processor design. This computation parallelizes over tensor contractions and thus takes an hour at most per design point on a single GPU, enabling rapid design iterations of the full array. Combining these effective models with semiclassical sampling, we then predict the quench dynamics of 100 qubits and 180 couplers at half filling, a sector of dimension $10^{29}$, and validate the approach against exact dynamics of smaller arrays. We show that our approach captures relaxation, thermalization, and transport, but not the bitstring statistics underlying cross-entropy benchmarks. The predicted transport carries a fingerprint of the device: under a staggered detuning, excitations cross over from ballistic to diffusive spreading, slow down at a doublon resonance, and diffuse at different rates on each sublattice. Our results chart which observables lie within classical reach and offer a practical tool for designing future devices.
2611.25053.why: Non-perturbative effective Hamiltonians for a 96-transmon coupler array at polynomial cost predict couplings, ZZ and quench dynamics.

eli5.plain: They show how to compute, on an ordinary computer, the effective interactions between qubits in a 96-qubit chip.
eli5.how: Continuous unitary transformations eliminate couplers and higher levels step by step, producing effective qubit couplings and residual ZZ terms without perturbation theory, at a cost polynomial in qubit number.
eli5.matters: Device models are what calibration and advantage claims rest on; a scalable non-perturbative method is useful for every tunable-coupler processor.
eli5.caveat: Accuracy is checked against simulation, not a measured device, and the model leaves out fabrication spread and noise.

2611.24605.title: Number-correlated photon entanglement with a quantum memory interferometer
2611.24605.abstract: Strong photon-photon interactions are central to quantum optical technologies yet remain challenging to realise at the single-photon level. Here, we show how embedding a quantum memory within a Mach-Zehnder interferometer enables a coherent transformation that converts single-mode photon states into number-correlated entangled states. Using an off-resonant ladder-type atomic interaction, storage and retrieval within a quantum memory maps a single-photon excitation onto a pair of photons across distinct optical modes via a driving control field. Embedding this within an interferometer deterministically produces an effective transformation in the photon number basis: $\sum_n a_n |n\rangle \to \sum_n a_n |n\rangle |n\rangle$ without relying on conventional optical nonlinearities. Measurement of one mode enables photonic non-demolition detection, state preparation, and frequency conversion as applications of the same underlying transformation. These results establish quantum memories embedded within an interferometric architecture as a platform for measurement-induced photon-photon interactions and the generation of Gaussian and non-Gaussian entangled states.
2611.24605.why: A quantum memory inside a Mach-Zehnder maps photon number n to |n⟩|n⟩ deterministically, giving non-demolition photon detection without optical nonlinearity.

eli5.plain: They propose a trick that copies the number of photons in one beam onto a second beam, entangling them, using a stored-light atomic memory instead of a nonlinear crystal.
eli5.how: Storing and retrieving light in a ladder-type atomic memory turns one excitation into a photon pair in two modes; putting this in an interferometer makes the map coherent for every photon number.
eli5.matters: Number-correlated entanglement and QND counting are what microwave photon counters and cat-state tools try to do; the interferometric idea might map to cQED memories.
eli5.caveat: A proposal; real memory efficiency and noise will degrade the deterministic map, especially for higher photon numbers.

2611.18839.title: Universal Quantum Computation in a Wigner's Friend Framework
2611.18839.abstract: The Wigner's Friend thought experiment illustrates a core tension in quantum mechanics: an observer inside an isolated laboratory (the Friend) measures a definite outcome, while an external observer (Wigner) describes the laboratory as a coherent superposition. Here we show that this discrepancy, usually studied as a conflict between descriptions, has a direct computational consequence. We namely propose a protocol by which Wigner can turn the Friend's laboratory into a universal quantum computer, whereby the Friend is restricted to apply simple classical operations within the laboratory. We also experimentally implement a proof-of-principle demonstration of this protocol for single-qubit gates using single photons. By recasting the coherence between incompatible descriptions as a computational resource, we thus link the foundations of quantum measurement to quantum computation.
2611.18839.why: Wigner can turn the Friend's lab into a universal quantum computer while the Friend only does classical operations; single-photon demo for one-qubit gates.

eli5.plain: They turn the Wigner's friend paradox into a computer: the outside observer gets full quantum computing from a friend who only does classical steps inside a sealed lab.
eli5.how: Because Wigner treats the friend's measurement as a coherent unitary, combining it with Wigner's own operations generates universal gates; they show single-qubit gates with photons.
eli5.matters: It gives the observer-dependence of facts an operational, testable consequence that could be run on superconducting qubits with a qubit 'friend'.
eli5.caveat: The friend is a qubit, not an observer, so it sharpens rather than settles the interpretational question; the experiment covers single-qubit gates only.

2611.23418.title: Experimental constraints on gauge hidden-variable models in Bell tests
2611.23418.abstract: Quantum mechanics assigns identical statistics to measurement procedures that realize the same final effect, irrespective of the transformations used to reach it. We test this operational equivalence with polarization-entangled photons by implementing one of Bob's analyzer settings either directly or through closed wave-plate trajectories $C_γ$ calibrated to produce the same measurement operator. Motivated by ontological descriptions in which a hidden frame is transported between contexts, we formulate a local path-memory model and derive the mixed-context bound $|S_γ^{\rm mix}|\leq 2+2p_γ$. The quantity $p_γ$ is a coupling-dependent counterfactual mismatch probability: it bounds a contextual Bell expression, but neither generates nor predicts the quantum Bell correlation. We therefore test path memory through the observable difference between direct and looped implementations, using a no-signaling phenomenological response in which a hidden holonomy $δ_γ$ modifies one correlation term in $S_γ^{\rm mix}$. The direct reference violates the Bell inequality, while the looped mixed-context curves remain indistinguishable from it within the experimental precision. Our results support the quantum equivalence of calibrated measurement implementations and constrain path-sensitive hidden-variable extensions that predict an observable memory of the optical history.
2611.23418.why: Photon Bell test finds directly and loop-implemented equivalent analyzers indistinguishable, constraining path-memory hidden-variable models.

eli5.plain: They checked whether a measurement 'remembers' how the polarizer was set, by reaching the same setting directly or via a loop of wave-plate turns.
eli5.how: A path-memory hidden-variable model predicts a holonomy that changes one Bell correlation; looped and direct settings give the same Bell value within error.
eli5.matters: It is a clean null test of operational equivalence, the kind of control experiment that could also be run with microwave qubits.
eli5.caveat: It rules out only a specific class of path-sensitive models, and sensitivity is set by experimental precision.

2611.25095.title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
2611.25095.abstract: The realization of large-scale quantum computation will require quantum error correction (QEC). One way to reduce the demands placed on QEC is to correct dominant physical errors at a lower level before passing the remaining errors to an outer code. Recently, Krastanov et al. [Nat. Commun. 12, 191 (2021)] proposed a measurement-free error-correction protocol based on coherent control of photonic modes that corrects for photon loss. Here, we adapt this approach to a circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architecture using three superconducting microwave cavities coupled by Josephson-junction-based nonlinear elements. We encode the logical qubit in the lowest-order binomial code of one cavity, while the two other cavities serve as ancillas. Using numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters, we demonstrate that our protocol can correct single-photon loss with 99% fidelity. Furthermore, we optimize the waiting time between successive rounds of error-correction, and show that the logical lifetime can be extended by a factor of 1.2-1.8 relative to the unprotected Fock $\{|0\rangle, |1\rangle\}$ encoding, surpassing break-even performance. Our work highlights the potential of gate-based, measurement-free QEC for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
2611.25095.why: Adapts measurement-free photon-loss correction to three cavities and Josephson couplers, encoding a binomial code without mid-circuit readout.

eli5.plain: They design a way for microwave cavities to fix lost photons automatically, without ever measuring them.
eli5.how: Loss errors in a binomial-code cavity are mapped by coherent nonlinear couplings into an ancilla cavity, which carries the entropy away; no measurement or feedback is needed.
eli5.matters: Slow, invasive mid-circuit measurement is a pain in bosonic codes; autonomous inner-layer correction lightens the load on an outer code.
eli5.caveat: A proposal; the benefit depends on the extra cavities and couplers not adding more error than they remove.

2611.19570.title: Linear-optical nonlocality without postselection
2611.19570.abstract: Linear optics is one of the major platforms for quantum information processing and experimental tests of quantum foundations. This motivates a thorough exploration of its capabilities and limitations. In this paper we investigate the extent to which passive linear optics, when fed with single-photon Fock states and followed by postselection-free number-resolving measurements, can demonstrate nonlocality. These resources define BosonSampling, a computational model believed to have intermediate computational power, being neither classically simulable nor quantum universal. We prove that, when restricted to only two input photons, this system also has intermediate nonlocality capabilities, achieving a violation of the CHSH inequality no higher than $1+\sqrt{2}$. Although this value has appeared frequently in the literature as achievable, to our knowledge this is the first proof that it is maximal. We show that, as we increase the number of available photons, linear optics can produce violations arbitrarily close to Tsirelson's bound of $2\sqrt{2}$. Finally, we extend the analysis to tripartite nonlocality, leveraging well-known interferometric suppression laws to show how several tripartite inequalities can be violated in this setup beyond their bipartite bounds.
2611.19570.why: Proves 1+√2 is the maximal CHSH value for two photons in passive linear optics without postselection; more photons approach Tsirelson.

eli5.plain: They pin down how much Bell-inequality violation plain beam splitters and photon counters can produce without throwing data away.
eli5.how: With single photons in, linear optics, and number-resolving detection, they prove a CHSH ceiling of 1+√2 for two photons and show more photons approach 2√2.
eli5.matters: It is a clean statement about what passive interferometers can certify, relevant to any photonic nonlocality test, microwave or optical.
eli5.caveat: Ideal lossless optics and perfect detectors; practical violation will be lower.

2611.24743.title: Squeezed Cooling and Lasing with Cold Atoms in Cavity-QED
2611.24743.abstract: A squeezed laser undergoes a lasing transition into a squeezed cavity mode, where stimulated emission generates a bright coherent field with a laser-like coherence time while maintaining one field quadrature below the vacuum noise level. Here we propose an optical implementation that needs neither a nonlinear crystal nor injected squeezed light, based on engineered interactions between ensembles of rubidium atoms and a squeezed cavity mode via cavity-assisted Raman transitions. A first ensemble cools the cavity into a squeezed vacuum, a mechanism we term squeezed cooling, yielding up to 9 dB in the intracavity field, surpassing the 3 dB limit of optical parametric oscillators. Tuned for output instead, it reaches up to 18 dB of output squeezing. Incoherently pumping a second ensemble drives a lasing transition into the squeezed mode, emitting a bright beam with long coherence time and noise below vacuum spanning a megahertz-wide band, away from the sharp phase-diffusion peak of excess noise at the carrier frequency, and robust to relaxation oscillations. We characterize lasing thresholds, superradiant emission, and linewidth narrowing, and identify the experimentally accessible regime where the system exhibits the defining features of a squeezed laser.
2611.24743.why: Cavity-assisted Raman engineering with two Rb ensembles predicts squeezed cooling to 9 dB and a lasing transition into a squeezed mode.

eli5.plain: They propose a laser whose output beam is quieter than vacuum in one quadrature, made with atoms rather than a nonlinear crystal.
eli5.how: One atomic ensemble cools the cavity into squeezed vacuum by engineered Raman transitions; a second, pumped ensemble then lases into that squeezed mode.
eli5.matters: Reservoir-engineered squeezing has a direct microwave analogue with driven qubits and resonators.
eli5.caveat: Theory only; the predicted 9 to 18 dB depends on idealised atom-cavity parameters.

2611.24604.title: Measurement-order dependence bounds uncertainty, contextuality, steering, and Bell nonlocality
2611.24604.abstract: Two quantum measurements applied to the same input in opposite orders give two joint distributions of the same outcomes. For Lüders instruments we measure how far apart these order records can be, over all inputs, by their total-variation distance $\mathcal{T}$, their Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathcal{J}$ (in bits), and their squared Hellinger distance. These order scores vanish exactly when the measurements commute, and $\mathcal{T}=\|[A,B]\|/4$ for two binary sharp observables. Some pairs of bases exceed mutually unbiased bases in squared Hellinger score, and in odd dimensions in $\mathcal{J}$, although their minimal entropy sum is smaller. For projective measurements, a Maassen-Uffink bound $q>0$ implies $\mathcal{T}\ge1-2^{-q}$ and a positive lower bound on $\mathcal{J}$. Measuring all observables of a scenario in sequence defines a joint distribution, so violations of noncontextuality, steering, and Bell inequalities are bounded by distances between order records. For correlation Bell inequalities with binary sharp observables, the squared Bell operator is a symmetrized (Jordan) part minus tensor products of local commutators. If one party has two settings, the violation is bounded bilinearly in the two parties' order scores; we conjecture this bound in general. On Clifford realizations it would follow from a Hilbert-Schmidt variant of Grothendieck's inequality, which we prove when one party has at most three settings. For three binary sharp measurements, the violation of Bell's original inequality by a maximally entangled state equals an order effect in three-measurement records of the maximally mixed state minus four times an alternation probability. For the rank-one Klyachko-Can-Binicioğlu-Shumovsky pentagon on a qutrit, the violation is at most the largest product of the order scores of two crossing diagonals, with equality at the maximal violation.
2611.24604.why: Total-variation distance between measurement-order records equals ||[A,B]||/4 and bounds uncertainty, contextuality, steering and Bell violations.

eli5.plain: They measure how much the order of two measurements matters, and show that this order effect caps how 'quantum' correlations can be.
eli5.how: Compare the outcome statistics of A-then-B and B-then-A; the distance between them vanishes iff A and B commute, and Bell and contextuality violations are bounded by such distances.
eli5.matters: It ties nonclassicality to something directly measurable in sequential measurements, which is natural on qubits with mid-circuit readout.
eli5.caveat: Some bounds are conjectured in general and proved only for few settings; the physical reading beyond the inequalities is limited.

2611.23971.title: Quantum Mpemba effect in a driven-dissipative atom-waveguide coupled system
2611.23971.abstract: The quantum Mpemba effect (QME) describes the counterintuitive phenomenon in which a more strongly perturbed quantum system relaxes toward its steady state faster than a less perturbed one. Here, we investigate the QME in a weakly driven-dissipative atomic array coupled to a one-dimensional chiral waveguide. Starting from the steady state, we introduce a local quench by resetting a single atom to its ground state and examine the subsequent relaxation dynamics. We find that quenching atoms near the array boundaries induces faster initial relaxation through enhanced coupling to superradiant modes and direct photon emission into the waveguide, giving rise to an edge-enhanced QME. Strong directional decay further amplifies this effect by promoting the spatial accumulation of superradiant modes near the preferred boundary, leading to a skin-enhanced QME. At later times, relaxation is increasingly governed by long-lived subradiant modes localized predominantly in the bulk of the array. By coupling two atomic arrays with different interparticle spacings, we further demonstrate an interface-induced QME, where quenching an atom near the interface makes the system relax more slowly at early times but approach its steady state faster at later times, owing to weak participation in both superradiant and subradiant modes. Our findings reveal how the spatial structure of collective decay modes and directional dissipation jointly govern anomalous quantum relaxation, offering potential routes toward accelerated steady-state preparation in waveguide QED systems.
2611.23971.why: Atom arrays on a chiral waveguide show edge-, skin- and interface-enhanced quantum Mpemba relaxation set by super- and subradiant modes.

eli5.plain: They show that in a chain of emitters on a one-way waveguide, disturbing an atom at the edge can make the whole system settle faster.
eli5.how: Resetting one atom excites a mix of fast-decaying superradiant and slow subradiant collective modes; where you reset determines the mix, giving faster or slower relaxation.
eli5.matters: Waveguide QED with artificial atoms can realise chiral couplings; faster steady-state preparation is useful there.
eli5.caveat: Numerical study in the weak-drive regime; the 'Mpemba' framing is mostly a relaxation-rate comparison.

2611.26371.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
2611.26371.abstract: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint $X$-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.
2611.26371.why: Superposing two Zeno measurement schedules via a control qubit predicts visibility set only by time offset and a reversed Zeno trend.

eli5.plain: They propose a circuit where the timing of measurements is itself put in superposition, inspired by the idea that time is read from a quantum clock.
eli5.how: A schedule qubit controls which of two Zeno measurement sequences acts on a driven qubit; interference visibility depends only on their time offset, and conditioning reverses the Zeno trend.
eli5.matters: It is a concrete foundations experiment sized for a few superconducting qubits.
eli5.caveat: The link to Page-Wootters relational time is motivational; the predictions follow from ordinary controlled operations.

2611.19142.title: Excitation-Selective Control of Protected Subradiant Antiresonances
2611.19142.abstract: Subradiant cavity antiresonances exhibit narrow spectral features, yet controlling their nonlinear response without perturbing the protected resonance remains challenging. Here we demonstrate excitation-selective control of a subradiant antiresonance in a driven two-emitter cavity-QED system. An auxiliary collective channel leaves the antisymmetric single-excitation state unaffected while shifting the doubly excited state, introducing tunable excitation anharmonicity without altering the linear antiresonance. This separation enables control of two-photon excitation pathways and photon correlations. Independently, a spatial coupling phase tunes optical access to the subradiant state without changing its intrinsic decay rate. We find that the interferometric phase information per incident photon is optimized when cavity-induced readout approximately matches intrinsic subradiant decay, while steady-state atomic entanglement peaks at an intermediate coupling phase. We further extend phase-selective optical control to collective subradiant modes in correlated emitter arrays. These results establish collective symmetry and spatial mode matching as distinct controls of nonlinear photon correlations, optical phase information, and atomic entanglement.
2611.19142.why: An auxiliary collective channel shifts the two-excitation state of a two-emitter cavity without touching the subradiant antiresonance.

eli5.plain: They find a way to tune the nonlinear response of two emitters in a cavity while leaving their narrow dark-state feature intact.
eli5.how: An extra collective coupling shifts only the doubly excited state, and a spatial coupling phase controls access to the dark state.
eli5.matters: Two qubits in a cavity or waveguide are standard in cQED, so these knobs could be tried directly.
eli5.caveat: Theory; the advantage over existing dark-state control schemes is incremental.

W7225865627.title: Coherence degradation of a superconducting qubit induced by sustained drive via photonic link
W7225865627.abstract: Photonic links offer a promising route to mitigate the thermal bottleneck in large-scale superconducting quantum processors by reducing the heat load on the dilution refrigerator. However, their impact on the qubit coherence under sustained operation, which is essential for tasks such as spin locking and high-duty-cycle gates, remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate a superconducting transmon qubit driven sustainedly via a photonic link. In spin-locking measurements, we observe a remarkable increase in the relaxation rate under sustained drive. We increase the optical power incident on the photodiode and measure qubit coherence as a function of the applied power. Both the energy relaxation time (T1) and echo dephasing time (T2E) decrease monotonically with the increase of optical power. This degradation persists even after adding low-pass and infrared filters, ruling out the high-frequency noise above the resonator band as the dominant mechanism. We attribute the observed coherence degradation to the photocurrent shot noise from the detector, which heats the qubit environment and increases the density of thermally generated quasiparticles. Our findings reveal that while photonic links reduce passive heat load, the intrinsic shot noise of photodetection introduces a heating mechanism that may limit the qubit coherence under high-duty-cycle operation. Mitigating this effect will be critical for realizing the full potential of photonic links in large-scale quantum processors.
W7225865627.why: Sustained optical-link drive of a transmon raises relaxation under spin locking; coherence loss tracks photodiode power.

eli5.plain: They found that delivering qubit drive signals over optical fibre into the fridge hurts the qubit if the drive stays on for long.
eli5.how: A photodiode at low temperature converts light to microwaves; in spin-locking experiments relaxation grows with optical power, pointing to light- or quasiparticle-related heating.
eli5.matters: Photonic links are a leading answer to the wiring heat problem; this is a concrete warning for high-duty-cycle operation.
eli5.caveat: One device and one link design; the microscopic mechanism is inferred rather than isolated.

2611.21397.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
2611.21397.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from $-155\;$dBm to $-130\;$dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from $-95\;$dBm to $-55\;$dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of $6.0\;$GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of $(74.7\pm 0.2) \;$dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of $(75.4\pm 6.8) \;$dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.
2611.21397.why: Compares transmons sitting directly on the feedline with dispersively coupled ones as calibrated Rabi-frequency probes of on-chip microwave power at millikelvin.

eli5.plain: They used qubits as power meters to find out how much microwave power actually reaches a chip inside the fridge.
eli5.how: A qubit's Rabi oscillation rate is proportional to the field driving it, so measuring that rate gives the field amplitude; they compare qubits hanging straight on the line with qubits reached through a readout resonator.
eli5.matters: Every drive-strength, photon-number and attenuation estimate in cQED rests on knowing the power at the device; an in-situ calibration with a waveguide-coupled qubit is directly reusable.
eli5.caveat: Accuracy depends on knowing each qubit's coupling to the line, which itself comes from modelling or a separate fit; it is a calibration study, not new physics.

2611.19139.title: Spontaneous Chiral Superradiance of a Spin-1 Condensate in a Ring Cavity
2611.19139.abstract: We investigate superradiant phase transitions in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to a ring cavity, where two symmetry-related Raman processes couple the atomic spin states to counterpropagating cavity modes. Above the superradiant threshold, we find that the symmetry between the two Raman channels is spontaneously broken, giving rise to a chiral superradiant (CSR) phase. Despite the exchange symmetry of the Hamiltonian, the CSR state spontaneously selects one of the two propagation directions, with one cavity mode becoming macroscopically occupied while its counterpropagating partner remains dark. Spin-dependent collisions further reshape the superradiant phase diagram by selectively shifting the boundaries between the chiral and symmetric superradiant phases, a feature intrinsic to the multicomponent spin-$1$ manifold. For sufficiently negative spin-dependent interactions, the interaction-induced modification of the atomic level structure gives rise to a reversed plane-wave phase characterized by an inverted internal-state occupation. These results identify spontaneous selection between symmetry-related superradiant channels as a mechanism for generating chirality in many-body cavity QED and demonstrate how spin-dependent collisions control the resulting superradiant phase structure.
2611.19139.why: A spin-1 BEC in a ring cavity spontaneously picks one propagation direction, a chiral superradiant phase shaped by spin-dependent collisions.

eli5.plain: They predict that a cloud of atoms in a ring-shaped cavity will choose to emit light in one direction only, even though both are equally allowed.
eli5.how: Two symmetric Raman channels compete above the superradiant threshold, and the symmetry breaks spontaneously; atomic spin collisions move the phase boundaries.
eli5.matters: Spontaneous chirality is a new collective effect; the analogue in superconducting ring resonators is speculative.
eli5.caveat: Mean-field theory; no experimental signature beyond the phase diagram is proposed.

2611.22057.title: QCap: a physics-corrected graph neural network for the capacitance matrix of any planar superconducting device layout
2611.22057.abstract: Electromagnetic simulations of device layouts to extract capacitance are computationally intensive, a major obstacle to accurate design of circuit devices. Machine learning models can bypass these simulations, but previous approaches have been restricted to layouts using only particular components, and require thousands of simulations of those same components as training data. We present QCap, a model that accurately predicts the Maxwell capacitance matrix of an arbitrary superconducting device layout in seconds, compared to minutes to hours of Ansys Q3D simulations. We develop a novel design-embedding algorithm that converts the layout into a universal graph format, allowing the model to work with any layout created with any tool. To achieve high accuracy, we obtain a coarse physics prior from a fast method of moments simulation of capacitance, then train the model to correct this prior. On 4,009 test designs withheld from training data the model outputs agree with Q3D simulations to a median error of 0.177%, and on never-seen component families it stays below 1% error. We demonstrate the model's scaling by obtaining the capacitance matrix of a 9-superconducting-qubit device in 12 seconds on a laptop (compared to 19.9 h and 228 GB of memory in Ansys) with sub-percent error, and capacitance of a (too large to simulate) 100-qubit, 781-conductor device in 3.4 min on a laptop. We provide the open-source models and data on SQuADDS and Hugging Face. Our results provide a powerful tool for large-scale accurate circuit design and guide the development of models to bypass other physical simulations.
2611.22057.why: Graph neural network predicts the full Maxwell capacitance matrix of any planar layout in seconds, replacing Q3D runs.

eli5.plain: They trained a neural network to predict a chip layout's capacitances in seconds instead of hours of electromagnetic simulation.
eli5.how: Layouts are turned into a universal graph format, and a physics-corrected graph network outputs the capacitance matrix, generalising beyond the components it saw.
eli5.matters: Faster capacitance extraction shortens the design loop for every transmon or fluxonium layout.
eli5.caveat: Accuracy on genuinely new geometries and on non-planar features like airbridges is the open question.

2611.25323.title: Generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states in a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model implemented with Josephson junctions
2611.25323.abstract: We investigate the generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model (JCM) implemented in a Josephson-junction quantum circuit. We consider a specific superconducting flux-qubit implementation and estimate the resulting two-photon coupling constant. We numerically examine three types of noise: magnetic flux noise with $1/f$ fluctuations, energy relaxation associated with the flux-qubit $T_{1}$ decay, and photon loss in the bosonic mode obtained by quantizing the phase variable of the dc SQUID used for qubit readout. We find that photon loss has a particularly significant effect on cat-state fidelity. We also investigate the time evolution of the probability-amplitude distribution in the Pegg-Barnett phase-state basis for the $l$-photon JCM ($l=1,2,3,4$), starting from a coherent bosonic state. Finally, we assume that the bosonic mode is initially prepared in a displaced thermal state and then decoupled from the heat bath. We study the subsequent unitary evolution to determine how the initial temperature affects the fidelity and Wigner function of the generated cat states.
2611.25323.why: Flux-qubit two-photon Jaynes-Cummings coupling estimate shows cat-state generation is limited mainly by loss of the SQUID's bosonic mode.

eli5.plain: They work out whether a real superconducting circuit could make Schrödinger cat states of microwave light by trading photons two at a time with a qubit.
eli5.how: A flux qubit coupled to the plasma mode of a dc SQUID gives a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings interaction; they estimate its strength and simulate flux noise, qubit decay and photon loss.
eli5.matters: Two-photon exchange is a direct route to cat states without the usual Kerr or parametric drives, and the noise budget tells you which part of such a device to improve first.
eli5.caveat: Pure numerics on one assumed device; the coupling estimate has not been measured, and the readout SQUID mode is a lossy host for a cat.

2611.24861.title: Time-Varying Medium from an Ensemble of Laser-Dressed Quantum Emitters
2611.24861.abstract: We propose a minimal quantum-mechanical model of a frequency dispersive, time-modulated medium that explicitly incorporates the pumping mechanism. It consists of a homogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters dressed by a pump laser. We analyze their dispersive, time-varying response to a perturbative probe field by deriving the macroscopic polarizability of the ensemble, and then solving Maxwell's equations via the Floquet formalism. This yields a rich band structure that departs from conventional analyses in which the modulation source is neglected, arising from the interplay between the dispersive polaritonic and time-varying responses. These results shed light on the role of the modulation source in time-varying media and pave the way toward realizing dispersive time-varying media from driven quantum-mechanical systems.
2611.24861.why: Derives the macroscopic polarizability of a laser-dressed emitter ensemble, giving a time-varying medium with its pump included.

eli5.plain: They build a minimal quantum model of a material whose optical properties change in time because a pump laser drives it.
eli5.how: A homogeneous ensemble of emitters is dressed by a pump; its polarizability is derived and fed to Maxwell's equations via Floquet theory.
eli5.matters: Time-modulated media, like parametrically pumped microwave lines, need models that include the pump; this gives one.
eli5.caveat: Theory with a simple homogeneous ensemble; effects of disorder and saturation are not treated.

2611.25030.title: Passive memories beyond the Ising model: from SFQ to GKP
2611.25030.abstract: Self-correcting quantum memories are spin Hamiltonians that aim to generalize the classical memory of the magnetic hard disk (i.e. ferromagnetic Ising model) to protect against both bit flips and phase flips. Beyond the magnetic hard disk, there are other passive classical memories that are used in modern computers, notably: the flash memory in laptops (which traps charge on a conducting island), and the flux storage loop in single-flux quantum (SFQ) logic (which traps flux in a superconducting loop). In this paper we review how storage and writing work in these two classical memories, drawing analogies to the charge qubit and the flux qubit. Protection in these systems derives not from scaling a lattice to the thermodynamic limit, but from a large, tunable energy barrier that separates codewords during memory, yet can be suppressed during a write. Towards protecting a qubit: We introduce a 2D ``floating XY model'' that combines the exponential (phase-flip) protection of the floating charge island with the polynomial (bit-flip) protection of the ferromagnetic XY model. We also study a self-dual superconducting circuit that hosts GKP codewords as symmetry-broken ground states of a $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2 $-symmetric circuit, and discuss its protection and limitations.
2611.25030.why: Draws analogies from flash and SFQ flux memories to charge and flux qubits, sketching passive protection routes toward GKP-type memories.

eli5.plain: They ask what everyday computer memories, like flash and superconducting flux loops, can teach us about storing qubits passively.
eli5.how: They review how charge-trapping and flux-trapping memories store bits through energy barriers, not size, and map that to charge and flux qubits and bosonic codes.
eli5.matters: Passive, self-protecting memories are the dream behind protected circuits such as 0-pi and GKP; the analogy may suggest designs.
eli5.caveat: Mostly a conceptual review; no new device or concrete threshold is shown.

2611.26214.title: Cooperativity-enhanced single-photon emission in a topological quantum emitter chain
2611.26214.abstract: Single-photon emitters are one of the key elements in state-of-the art quantum technologies, yet optimizing and manipulating their emission requires precise fabrication of the emitter systems themselves. Here, we propose a route to tailored single-photon emission by exploiting cooperative effects in a topological single-photon emitter chain. Although the involvement of multiple emitters normally suppresses single-photon emission, we show that localized topological edge modes restore single-photon emission and protect against local perturbations. At the same time, cooperative effects occur due to the collective nature of the edge modes, leading to directional emission and linewidth narrowing. Our findings open new possibilities for tailoring single-photon emission by combining cooperativity and topological effects.
2611.26214.why: Topological edge modes in an emitter chain restore single-photon emission while adding directional emission and linewidth narrowing.

eli5.plain: They show that a chain of emitters arranged with a topological pattern can still give out single photons, protected from local defects.
eli5.how: Normally many emitters spoil single-photon emission, but localised topological edge modes behave like one emitter while borrowing collective linewidth narrowing and directionality.
eli5.matters: Topological arrays of qubits on waveguides are buildable in circuits, so the idea is testable there.
eli5.caveat: Proposal; robustness to realistic disorder is shown only for local perturbations.

2611.20194.title: Quantum-Enhanced Passive and Active Radio-Frequency Photonic Imaging
2611.20194.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) photonics enables broadband, phase-coherent sensing beyond the reach of purely electronic architectures, yet at a given optical carrier power its sensitivity is bounded by the standard quantum limit of the optical readout. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that this limit can be surpassed in both passive and active RF imaging modalities by encoding RF signals onto a bright phase-squeezed optical carrier and recovering them via balanced homodyne detection, while the RF front end, illumination, and image reconstruction remain classical. A unified measurement model shows that phase squeezing reduces the variance of the additive readout noise by a single factor $g$, yielding peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gains of up to $2G$, where $G\equiv10\log_{10}(1/g)$: between $G$ and $2G$ for deterministic targets in active imaging when the classical noise of the echoes is negligible against the readout noise, and set by the ratio of scene noise to readout noise in passive imaging. We validate the model in an experiment in the 5--20 MHz band, in which synthesized RF scenes are replayed through a physical squeezed-light receiver. With 3 dB of squeezing, the PSNR improves by about 6 dB, close to $2G$, in the readout-noise-dominated regime of both modalities, and the model predicts the measured gains without free parameters. These results identify where squeezed-light readout benefits RF-photonic imaging: wherever the optical readout noise, rather than the scene or the RF front end, dominates the image error.
2611.20194.why: Phase-squeezed optical carrier beats the standard quantum limit in passive and active RF photonic imaging.

eli5.plain: They used squeezed light to make radio-frequency imaging less noisy than the normal quantum limit allows.
eli5.how: RF signals are written onto a phase-squeezed optical beam and read out by balanced homodyne detection, leaving the RF front end unchanged.
eli5.matters: A practical squeezing application outside the lab; the analogous microwave squeezing is the reader's daily work.
eli5.caveat: Improvement is modest and limited by optical losses; 'another squeezing gain' rather than a new mechanism.

2611.23383.title: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction
2611.23383.abstract: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks. Mechanically mediated transducers, however, remain limited by weak electromechanical coupling, dissipation, and added noise. In this work, we study a transducer in which an ensemble of superconducting qubits couples collectively to a shared optomechanical resonator. For weak signals, we show that ensemble size and optical pump strength together set the conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth, with pump heating limiting efficiency to a finite optimal pump strength. Near half excitation, the collective coupling grows nearly linearly with ensemble size, accelerating transfer of an excitation into the mechanics. We show that this speedup is offset by relaxation of the additional excited qubits, so the single-qubit coupling and lifetime still set the coherence requirement. Transferring exactly one excitation also requires an anharmonic mechanical mode, which an auxiliary qubit coupled to the mechanics can provide. In a lossless prescribed-Kerr benchmark with four qubits and $g_{\rm sm}/(2π)=3.81\,\mathrm{kHz}$, a mechanical anharmonicity of $100\,\mathrm{kHz}$ raises the final joint single-photon intracavity target probability from $19.6\%$ to $99.7\%$. Finally, we quantify the effects of decoherence, disorder, residual qubit--qubit interactions, and pump-induced qubit noise, finding that pair-dependent interactions reduce the optical retrieval efficiency from 58\% to 35\%. These results establish the coherence and selectivity requirements for collective quantum transduction.
2611.23383.why: An ensemble of qubits coupled collectively to one optomechanical resonator raises microwave-to-optical conversion efficiency, with pump heating setting an optimal pump.

eli5.plain: They propose using many superconducting qubits together, rather than one circuit, to talk to a vibrating mechanical element that converts microwave signals to light.
eli5.how: The qubits share one mechanical mode, so their coupling adds up collectively; near half excitation the collective coupling grows almost linearly with qubit number while the optical pump heats the device.
eli5.matters: Transduction is the bottleneck for linking fridges optically; a collective interface is a knob that existing piezo-optomechanical transducers do not use.
eli5.caveat: Theory only, and it assumes many identical, well-controlled qubits on the transducer; added noise from real pump heating may be worse than modelled.

2611.14427.title: Tuning and Mapping of Two-Tone Optomechanical Instability up to the Physical Limits
2611.14427.abstract: We report on the compete theory describing the two-tone instability proper to optomechanical back-action-evading experiments. We address all possible mistunings (including power imbalance of the two pumps), as well as the device imperfections (finite mechanical quality factor, and sideband resolution). We illustrate the importance of power mistuning and sideband resolution, the latter being particularly relevant in finding the back-action-evading "sweet spot". The model is compared to experiments performed up to an extremely high cooperativity, of almost a 100. This has been made possible thanks to a fine-tuning procedure, which is presented. The agreement theory-experiment is very good, and the limiting factor is unraveled: cavity frequency noise. Besides, we discover at very high drive powers new self-driven states, which all share the characteristic feature of presenting a mechanical comb spectrum; as if the synchronization of the responses to the two drives (which occurs at lower powers) was destroyed by nonlinear effects. We believe that our work is extremely relevant to the implementation of back-action-evading experiments, as well as other related two-tone schemes.
2611.14427.why: Complete theory of two-tone optomechanical instability with all mistunings, compared to experiments at very high cooperativity.

W7234724128.title: Scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy of Re-capped Nb Films: A materials perspective on capping layers for superconducting circuits
W7234724128.abstract: Thin metal capping layers on the surface of Niobium (Nb) capacitor pads in transmon qubits have been shown to reduce RF losses in the Nb oxide and increase the T1 decay time. Here, we demonstrate that low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) uniquely enables simultaneous nanoscale imaging of the surface morphology and local superconducting density of states (DOS) on the capping layers with sub-nanometer resolution, providing insight into properties relevant to qubit performance. We investigate Nb/Re, where rhenium (Re) is chosen as the capping layer due to its minimal surface oxidation after air exposure. Spectroscopic measurements show large, spatially uniform superconducting regions with near ideal, BCS-like DOS, characterized by zero conductance at zero bias and an effective gap parameter reasonably close to that of the underlying Nb film, consistent with a proximity effect model in the diffuse limit. At the same time, STM/STS uncovers two key microscopic mechanisms that are not accessible to conventional surface-analysis techniques. First, the Re overlayer exhibits a granular, fibrous morphology that correlates with a reduced effective gap in some regions, providing direct evidence that the capping layer can be permeable and can degrade superconducting properties through nanoscale structural inhomogeneity. Second, we identify nanoscale defect regions hosting pronounced sub-gap quasiparticle resonances, Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (Shiba) states, consistent with Kondo scattering from localized magnetic moments. Combined with time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) measurements, these observations indicate the formation of NbOx clusters at the Re surface, demonstrating that oxidation loss channels can persist even in capped structures. These results provide materials guidance for improving capping layers in superconducting qubit circuits.
W7234724128.why: STM/STS on rhenium-capped niobium shows a uniform proximity gap at sub-nanometre resolution, informing capping layers for higher-T1 transmons.

eli5.plain: They looked at qubit metal surfaces atom by atom to see whether a protective rhenium coat on niobium stays superconducting everywhere.
eli5.how: Low-temperature scanning tunnelling spectroscopy maps both the surface shape and the local density of superconducting states on the cap.
eli5.matters: Capping niobium has recently raised T1; this explains what the surface actually looks like electronically.
eli5.caveat: No qubits measured here, so the link to coherence is indirect.

2611.22546.title: Multilevel Effects and the Limits of the Quantum Rabi Model in Ultrastrong Coupling system
2611.22546.abstract: The spectrum of artificial atoms coupled to resonators in the ultrastrong coupling regime have been analyzed using the quantum Rabi model over a wide range of coupling strengths. However, the accuracy of models obtained by truncating multilevel artificial atoms to two levels, as well as the correspondence between effective parameters extracted from spectral fitting and the bare parameters of the circuit Hamiltonian, depends on the multilevel structure of the system. In this study, I analyze the spectrum of an ultrastrongly coupled circuit consisting of a multilevel superconducting artificial atom and a resonator using a circuit Hamiltonian, and investigate the effects of truncating higher atomic levels on the low-energy spectrum. Based on Löwdin partitioning, I evaluate the contributions of virtual transitions through higher atomic levels and show that diagonal energy corrections reduce the errors arising from simple two-level truncation over a wide parameter range. I also show that there are parameter regimes in which readjustment of the effective Rabi parameters successfully reproduces the multilevel spectrum, while systematic deviations remain in other regimes. These results demonstrate the necessity of separately evaluating two-level truncation, perturbative corrections, and effective-parameter fitting in ultrastrongly coupled systems, and provide guidance for quantitative spectral analysis of multilevel quantum circuits.
2611.22546.why: Circuit-Hamiltonian analysis shows where truncating an ultrastrongly coupled artificial atom to two levels makes quantum Rabi model fits misleading.

eli5.plain: They check when it is fair to treat an ultrastrongly coupled superconducting atom as a two-level system.
eli5.how: Starting from the full circuit Hamiltonian of a multilevel atom plus resonator, they compare its spectrum with truncated Rabi-model fits and track how fitted parameters drift from the bare circuit values.
eli5.matters: Ultrastrong-coupling claims in circuits are usually backed by Rabi-model fits; this says how much to trust the extracted coupling g.
eli5.caveat: Single-author theory on a model circuit; how large the error is in a given experiment depends on its specific anharmonicity.

2611.23046.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
2611.23046.abstract: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. Additionally, individual cavities can be independently brought into resonance with NV zero-phonon lines on the same chip. These results combine bulk-like optical coherence with frequency multiplexing and cavity-enhanced emission, establishing a scalable nanophotonic platform for NV-based quantum network nodes.
2611.23046.why: NV centres in one diamond nanocavity keep 19 MHz linewidths, enabling frequency multiplexing of Purcell-enhanced emitters.

2611.21869.title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
2611.21869.abstract: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.
2611.21869.why: Tripartite exciton-polariton, magnon and phonon coupling in suspended CrSBr membranes near 20 GHz.

2611.22798.title: How can every physicist become a Bohmian
2611.22798.abstract: The Bohmian interpretation of quantum mechanics is controversial because it attributes deterministic trajectories to microscopic particles. We propose a reformulation that sidesteps this controversy: rather than applying Bohmian mechanics at the microscopic level, we recast it as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus, with no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world. In this form, the Bohmian trajectory becomes a practical tool for visualizing the emergence of a definite measurement outcome, broadly acceptable to physicists who would otherwise reject the Bohmian program.
2611.22798.why: Recasts Bohmian mechanics as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer only, dropping microscopic trajectories.

eli5.plain: They suggest using Bohmian trajectories only for the needle of a measuring device, not for particles.
eli5.how: The pointer's position is treated as a hidden deterministic variable guided by the wavefunction, which visualises how a single outcome emerges.
eli5.matters: It offers a pragmatic picture of measurement that avoids the most contested Bohmian claims.
eli5.caveat: It is a reinterpretation with no new prediction, so it changes presentation rather than physics.

W7236011103.title: Optimal control of a fluxonium circuit with the Q-PRONTO numerical method
W7236011103.abstract: Optimizing the control of large quantum systems is a resource-intensive task, where the convergence rate of the underlying iterative schemes is crucial. The recently developed Quantum Projection Operator-Based Newton Method for Trajectory Optimization (Q-PRONTO) offers a unique quadratic convergence for controlling quantum states, while most model-based solvers guarantee only an approximately linear convergence rate. As a proof of concept, here, we design and benchmark single-qubit gates optimized by Q-PRONTO based on the circuit Hamiltonian of a fluxonium superconducting qubit. To ensure that we can apply a long string of arbitrary pulses to the circuit, we modify the firmware associated with the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) by altering its memory allocation. We characterize the performance of the optimal solutions using standard randomized benchmarking and achieve a total error per gate of 6.6 × 10 − 4 .
W7236011103.why: Q-PRONTO quadratic-convergence optimal control designs fluxonium single-qubit pulses and runs them after firmware changes for long arbitrary pulse strings.

eli5.plain: They used a fast-converging optimiser to design control pulses for a fluxonium qubit and ran them on hardware.
eli5.how: A Newton-type trajectory optimiser works on the full circuit Hamiltonian and converges quadratically; firmware was modified to play long arbitrary pulse sequences.
eli5.matters: Fluxonium gates are sensitive to leakage through higher levels; model-based control with quick convergence helps.
eli5.caveat: Proof of concept on single-qubit gates; no fidelity record or comparison with standard DRAG-style pulses at scale.

W7236565036.title: Sideband frequency comb generation phase diagram in a high-impedance superconducting resonator
W7236565036.abstract: We explore frequency comb generation (FCG) and sideband FCG (sb-FCG) in a high-impedance superconducting NbTiN thin film λ/2 coplanar waveguide resonator. Primary frequency comb generation is governed by an underlying four-wave mixing process in a measured frequency band in the 1−11 GHz range. Sb-FCG occurs around the primary comb teeth at distinct microwave frequency and power values that follow sharp discontinuities in the high-power microwave transmission and obey higher-order wave mixing processes. We map the FCG and sb-FCG as a function of pump frequency and applied microwave power, uncovering a “phase diagram” for the presence of the sb-FCG. The device simplicity and bandwidth make it a potential new platform for scalable frequency-multiplexing readout of superconducting qubits.
W7236565036.why: Maps when sideband combs appear around four-wave-mixing comb teeth in a high-impedance NbTiN resonator, giving a pump-power/frequency phase diagram.

eli5.plain: They drive a simple superconducting resonator hard and map when it spits out a comb of evenly spaced frequencies, and when extra combs appear around each tooth.
eli5.how: The kinetic-inductance nonlinearity of a high-impedance NbTiN line causes four-wave mixing; higher-order mixing produces sidebands at sharp jumps in transmission, which they chart versus pump frequency and power.
eli5.matters: Kinetic-inductance resonators are common in parametric amplifiers and detectors; knowing where they go unstable is practical for anyone pumping them.
eli5.caveat: Classical nonlinear optics in a microwave resonator, with no quantum measurements; the sideband mechanism is described rather than fully modelled.

2611.21999.title: Transient Synchronization and Entanglement through Shared Dissipation in Circuit QED
2611.21999.abstract: We propose a superconducting circuit in which two resonators couple through DC-biased SQUIDs to a common lossy auxiliary mode. Adiabatic elimination yields collective damping and correlated noise with an overlap $ξ$ whose magnitude is tuned by the flux biases and whose sign follows the relative sign of the couplings. The full three-mode dynamics confirm this reduced description. For detuned resonators, we derive the exceptional-point condition, above which the mean amplitudes lock to a common frequency. For resonant modes, unequal collective decay produces transient synchronization, antiphase or in phase depending on the relative sign of the couplings, with an analytical synchronization time set by the collective decay splitting and the initial mean amplitudes. For initially separable squeezed states, the same relaxation converts local squeezing into transient entanglement, quantified by logarithmic negativity. We obtain closed-form expressions for the squeezing threshold above which entanglement appears and for the time at which it disappears. Thermal noise suppresses entanglement without changing the mean-amplitude synchronization time at fixed parameters. For realistic circuit parameters, these effects occur within a few hundred nanoseconds and are accessible through output-field measurements. A single tunable shared channel thus produces an exceptional point, transient synchronization, and transient entanglement, and provides a controllable source of correlated noise for superconducting circuits.
2611.21999.why: Proposes two resonators coupled via SQUIDs to a shared lossy mode, predicting sign-tunable transient synchronization and dissipation-driven entanglement.

eli5.plain: They propose making two microwave resonators lock to a common rhythm and become entangled by letting both leak into the same lossy mode.
eli5.how: Eliminating the fast lossy mode leaves correlated damping whose sign and size are set by the SQUID flux biases; unequal collective decay then pulls the two resonators in or out of phase.
eli5.matters: Engineered shared dissipation is a standard cQED tool, and a flux-tunable sign gives a simple handle on collective decay.
eli5.caveat: Theory only; the entanglement is transient and the protocol needs good control of the SQUID couplings.

2611.18755.title: Directional gate-error asymmetry and universal selectivity bounds in non-unital open quantum systems
2611.18755.abstract: Clifford randomized benchmarking and average gate fidelity assign a single trajectory-independent decay rate to a noisy quantum gate at leading order in the dimensionless damping exposure \varepsilon = γT, concealing state-dependent transition-error asymmetries in untwirled quantum circuits. While state-dependent amplitude-damping errors are well known in open quantum systems, a trajectory-level analytical framework that bounds directional transition selectivity across arbitrary pulse shapes and Markovian environments has been lacking. Using first-order toggling-frame perturbation theory for a two-level qubit coupled to a Markovian bath, we show that the antipodal survival-error slopes χ_+ and χ_- along any piecewise-continuous control path depend exclusively on its time-averaged Bloch vector m and transverse residence covariance matrix G, obeying the complete-positivity cofactor bound β(r) \le 1. On a standard polar \sqrt{X} gate, longitudinal T_1 relaxation induces a 12.23 : 1 directional survival-error split (κ_{T_1} = (3π- 8)/(3π+ 8) \approx 0.081767), whereas time-symmetric X rotations maintain an exact 1 : 1 balance (κ_{T_1} = 1). Across all completely positive Markovian generators, coupling between non-unital drift and unital diffusion enforces a selectivity bound κ_\star = (π- 2\sqrt{2})/(π+ 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.052456 (19.06 : 1) for time-independent single-qubit πswaps. We apply this framework to Gaussian and derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) waveforms on superconducting transmons and trapped-ion qubits, extend the analysis to finite damping, pulse dwell, colored thermal baths, and qutrit leakage, and construct two-branch differential lock-in protocols that isolate directional error splits immune to first-order state-preparation and measurement errors.
2611.18755.why: Shows randomized benchmarking hides direction-dependent amplitude-damping errors and bounds that asymmetry across pulse shapes.

eli5.plain: They point out that a single average gate error hides that errors going up and going down can be very different.
eli5.how: First-order toggling-frame theory for a qubit in a Markovian bath gives slopes for survival errors from each pole and universal bounds on their ratio.
eli5.matters: Untwirled circuits feel these asymmetries; it matters for error models used in mitigation.
eli5.caveat: Single-author theory on a two-level model; the effect of amplitude damping asymmetry is well known qualitatively.

2611.20667.title: Near-synchronous multiphoton quantum interference
2611.20667.abstract: Nonclassical multiphoton interference is an important resource for optical quantum information processing, and its output statistics depend on the distinguishability of the input photons. In this paper, using time delay as a tunable parameter, we theoretically analyze the interference behavior of independent pure-state single photons with identical Gaussian spectral envelopes under near-synchronous conditions. Using the immanant representation of the single-photon internal-state overlap matrix to express the weights of the exchange-symmetry components, we determine the leading asymptotic behavior and approximation error of each weight, and characterize the weight suppression laws when different groups of photons become synchronized on different scales. Given the local identity classes of the delay functions and the vanishing orders of pairwise delay differences, the vanishing orders of the weights of the exchange-symmetry components can be computed in polynomial time by integer minimum-cost flow. On this basis, we provide a network-independent total-variation error bound for the complete output photon-number distribution, establish a quantitative relationship among the photon spectral width, synchronization precision, and interference statistics deviation, and provide a quantitative basis for the analysis and approximation of near-synchronous multiphoton interference.
2611.20667.why: Immanant analysis of multiphoton interference versus small time delays for identical Gaussian single photons.

W7235984709.title: History-Recovery Distance as an Operational Arrow of Time
W7235984709.abstract: Reduced-state distinguishability can revive and entropy can oscillate in non-Markovian dynamics. Thus, instantaneous states may not fully capture irreversibility. As histories unfold, causal consequences may spread across environmental records and multitime correlations beyond local recovery control. This mismatch can yield operational irreversibility despite reversible joint dynamics, even when reduced states recur. We therefore propose history recoverability as an operational perspective on irreversibility, describing multitime histories through process tensors under specified control. The optimal operational gap between ideal history reversal and admissible recoveries defines the history-recovery distance. We establish conditional monotonicity for causal extensions of a common physical realisation under compatible accessibility, recovery resources, and nested multitime testers. A three-qubit model shows reduced-state distinguishability revival alongside an increasing history-recovery distance under compatible constraints. Independent optimisation over the complete admissible recovery class yields positive increments across sampled parameters. Whether this ordering extends beyond these conditions, or admits counterexamples, remains open. These model-specific results motivate a proposed superconducting-qubit experiment. More broadly, a conceptual hierarchy relates history-level, state-level, statistical, entropic, and thermodynamic descriptions through operational sufficiency, coarse-graining, and additional reference-state and dynamical conditions. These connections suggest that different manifestations of operational irreversibility may share a common origin in the causal delocalisation of recovery-relevant information beyond accessible control.
W7235984709.why: Defines irreversibility as the gap between ideal history reversal and admissible recoveries on process tensors.

eli5.plain: They propose measuring the arrow of time by how well a whole history, not just the current state, can be undone.
eli5.how: Using process tensors for multitime correlations, they define a distance between perfect history reversal and the best allowed recovery.
eli5.matters: Non-Markovian qubit environments show revivals that confuse state-based irreversibility measures; this gives an alternative.
eli5.caveat: Conceptual proposal; operational meaning depends on the chosen set of allowed controls.

2611.21593.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
2611.21593.abstract: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.
2611.21593.why: InAs/EuS/Al nanowire junctions show a gate-tunable, hysteretic anomalous Josephson phase with remanent bias at zero field.

eli5.plain: They built junctions where a magnet layer gives the superconducting phase a built-in offset that a gate voltage can tune.
eli5.how: A SQUID interferometer measures the phase shift as field and gate are swept; simulations tie it to spin-orbit coupling.
eli5.matters: A zero-field, gate-controlled phase battery could bias flux circuits without coils.
eli5.caveat: Materials physics; hysteresis and history dependence make it far from a clean circuit element yet.

2611.24358.title: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains
2611.24358.abstract: We investigate the spontaneous emission of a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By tuning the chain from a metallic to a semiconducting character through dimerization, we analyze how the electronic structure of an atomic-scale scatterer, together with the illumination profile, determines the strength, bandwidth, and spatial structure of the spontaneous emission enhancement. The resonant enhancement depends on both spectral matching and the emitter position relative to the induced charge and field patterns. In metallic chains, the nearly harmonic energy spectrum leads to overlapping optical transitions and strong resonances. For semiconducting chains, dimerization opens a gap and leads to a modified density of electronic states, redistributing the response over a broader spectral range and reducing its peak intensity. Coulomb interactions affect the optical resonances through blueshift or modification of their spatial character, and act differently on collective and single-particle-like excitations. Finally, we show that the same mechanisms demonstrated in atomic chains persist in realistic quasi-one-dimensional systems, including trans-polyacetylene chains and graphene nanoribbons. Our findings indicate a general direction for engineering light-matter interactions at the atomic scale, and may offer design principles for tunable nanoscale photonic and quantum-optical devices.
2611.24358.why: Spontaneous emission enhancement near SSH atomic chains depends on metallic versus semiconducting dimerization.

2611.26315.title: All Non-Contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are Free-Fermion in Disguise
